name: Acetic Acid vs. Sodium Hydroxide
description: Standard analytical weak-acid strong-base titration illustrating the Henderson-Hasselbalch buffer zone and basic equivalence point (~8.72).
ghsAlert: Corrosive / Irritant: Wear safety goggles. Acetic acid vapors cause respiratory irritation.
prepNote: Standardize NaOH secondary standard against potassium hydrogen phthalate (KHP) prior to quantitative titration.

name: Hydrochloric Acid vs. Sodium Hydroxide
description: Classical monoprotic strong acid-strong base titration with a sharp vertical inflection passing directly through neutral pH 7.00.
ghsAlert: Corrosive: Concentrated HCl produces acidic fumes. NaOH causes severe chemical eye and skin burns.
prepNote: Always add acid to water when preparing stock dilutions. Stir continuously.

name: Ammonia vs. Hydrochloric Acid
description: Titration of a volatile weak base with strong mineral acid. Yields an acidic equivalence point (~5.28) due to ammonium cation hydrolysis.
ghsAlert: Toxic / Corrosive: Prepare ammonia stock solutions inside a certified chemical fume hood.
prepNote: Use Methyl Orange or Methyl Red; avoid Phenolphthalein due to premature color transition before equivalence.

name: Formic Acid vs. Sodium Hydroxide
description: Methanoic acid titration with a lower pKa buffer midpoint, showing steeper early buffering behavior.
ghsAlert: Corrosive / Flammable: Causes severe skin burns and eye damage.
prepNote: Rinse glassware with boiled deionized water to prevent dissolved CO2 from shifting the endpoint.
